assessment.scope: Schema and evidence references checked. Model prose is advisory and unverified; no acceptance or deployment authority.

response.summary: The discovery measurements support experiments on setup amortization, polynomial-state reuse, convergence-check overhead, and loop allocations. These are hypotheses only; no candidate has been tested or shown to improve performance.

opportunities.hypothesis: Application setup dominates these fresh-process measurements: setup medians are 0.5499960000161082 and 0.55117362504825 seconds, compared with sequence medians of 0.002617292106151581 and 0.0011215000413358212 seconds. Amortizing setup could matter if the actual workload repeatedly starts processes.
opportunities.proposed_change: Conditionally experiment with retaining an initialized application across requests. Separately investigate import, factory, and synchronization contributions before proposing targeted startup changes.
opportunities.validation: Measure setup and synchronized call sequences separately in fresh processes, then measure the explicitly defined persistent lifecycle. Verify request isolation and output equivalence. Establish deployment lifecycle before prioritizing this experiment.

opportunities.hypothesis: The supplied wrapper constructs a new algorithm instance per invocation. The batch profile records eight calls each to polyvander, pinv, and svd, suggesting repeated polynomial setup may be avoidable when inputs governing that setup match. The excerpts do not establish whether all weighted pseudoinverses are reusable.
opportunities.proposed_change: Experiment with retaining an algorithm instance for compatible calls and using its existing polynomial cache. Determine invalidation requirements for the x grid, polynomial order, weights, dtype, and peak masking before extending caching.
opportunities.validation: Compare the original and retained-instance paths on both supplied cases using clean synchronized timings. Check exact outputs, coefficients when returned, weights, tolerance histories, and iteration counts. Exercise changed setup inputs and ensure earlier returned arrays are not mutated by later calls. Measure retained-memory cost separately.

opportunities.hypothesis: Repeated convergence checks are a plausible source of dispatch overhead: the batch profile records 120 relative_difference calls and 240 norm calls; the single case records 15 and 30. The generic norm path may do unnecessary work for already validated vectors, although aggregate asarray counts cannot be attributed entirely to this path.
opportunities.proposed_change: Experiment with a narrowly scoped convergence-check path for the array shape and norm used by modpoly, retaining the general helper elsewhere. Preserve denominator flooring and stopping semantics; do not relax tolerance or reduce iterations as a performance shortcut.
opportunities.validation: Compare clean end-to-end timings and separately profile whether norm and conversion overhead decreases. Check exact baseline values, full tolerance histories, and iteration counts first. Any changed reduction order or norm implementation can alter rounding, overflow behavior, and threshold crossings; assess such differences against an explicit numerical contract before acceptance.

opportunities.hypothesis: The modpoly loop creates arrays for clipping, weighting, baseline evaluation, and differences. Its leading host self-time and traced live peaks justify an allocation experiment, but neither measurement proves allocation or memory bandwidth is the bottleneck. The single-call traced peak is 630494 bytes above start; batch call peaks range from 157548 to 160449 bytes.
opportunities.proposed_change: Experiment with reusable clipping and weighting scratch arrays, then consider alternating baseline buffers. Preserve baseline_old until convergence evaluation and preserve the original input when use_original is enabled.
opportunities.validation: Measure clean synchronized timings and separate traced live peaks and retention. Verify input immutability, output ownership, repeated-call isolation, optional branches, exact outputs, and convergence histories. Buffer reuse must not change aliasing or floating-point evaluation order unintentionally.

limitations: Only the supplied discovery cases were assessed. Case counts and call counts do not establish production frequency, workload mix, or compatible inputs for reuse.

cProfile and tracemalloc ran separately from clean timings. Their overhead can disproportionately affect short calls and alter hotspot rankings; profile times are not clean latency estimates. Nested cumulative times must not be added together.

The single-spectrum clean samples range from 0.001106291078031063 to 0.0033222080674022436 seconds. More controlled repetitions would be needed to distinguish candidate effects from variability; no speedup forecast is supported.
Continuation calls may perform different work, and observation between calls can perturb caches. Lower later-call timings do not establish a warmup benefit.

RSS is a lifetime process high-water mark including imports and fixtures. Tracemalloc measures traced live allocations, not total allocation traffic, copying, or device memory. Retained allocations do not establish a leak; device kernel attribution is unavailable.

Exact observed repeatability applies to the existing implementation and supplied cases. Changes to reductions, solver algorithms, dtype, or operation ordering can change floating-point results and convergence decisions.

Setup excludes interpreter and harness imports; timed calls include completion synchronization. Fixture loading, fingerprinting, and observer hooks are outside call timers. No files were changed and no optimization was tested or accepted.
